content:
Mike J: Heads-up — we're still missing reliable log->trace linking for hosted API errors. Canary drops show a bunch of ERROR logs with no trace id attached. Can we align on a strategy? Specifically: should apps always emit trace IDs as structured fields, or can ingestion/collector stitch them for legacy logs? Tradeoffs (cost, accuracy, UX) please.

Anya P: +1 to app-level injection as primary. Propose canonical field `redwood.trace_id` to avoid collisions with customer fields named `trace_id` or `otel.trace_id`. SDKs can auto-inject from OpenTelemetry context so app teams don't need to think about it. :+1:

Devon: For legacy/third-party apps we can try collector-side enrichment. If the ingress/edge sees `traceparent` or `tracestate` headers we can promote to a resource attribute and add the field to logs during ingest. Works when the same process (or sidecar) observes both the header and the logs.

Lee: Big cost caveat — indexing a high-cardinality trace id across the entire log stream will explode storage and query costs. We should NOT index `redwood.trace_id` for every log. Proposal: index only for logs with `level >= ERROR` OR whitelist by route/service (e.g., `service: llm-runtime` or `route: /generate`). Otherwise store as an unindexed attribute.

sre-oncall: We burned budget last quarter when `request_id` accidentally got indexed cluster-wide. Agrees with selective indexing + shorter retention on indexed docs. Suggestion: keep indexed trace links for 30d, raw log blob for 90d cold storage.

Mike J: What about heuristic stitching? e.g., match logs to traces by client_ip + small time window + request_path. That could help when headers are missing.

Anya P: Heuristics are brittle and can give false correlations. If we do fallback stitching, mark links as "inferred" and show confidence. Collector can best-effort attach `redwood.trace_id.inferred` but prefer app/SDK injection.

Devon: Example log JSON we'd like from SDKs (minimal):
```
{"ts":"2026-03-20T12:34:56Z","level":"error","service":"llm-runtime","msg":"model timeout","redwood.trace_id":"4f2b9c7e..."}
```
This keeps parser simple and enables direct console linking.

Anya P: Example OTEL collector processor we discussed (staging sketch):
```yaml
processors:
  redwood_trace_promote:
    match_headers: [traceparent, tracestate]
    action: extract_to_attribute
    attribute_name: redwood.trace_id
```
We'll refine to real collector syntax, but that's the behaviour we want.

infra-bot: FYI I created staging job: collector patch to insert `redwood.trace_id` from `traceparent` header in edge pool c-4. Deployed to staging at 1718206000. Logs show attribute present on ~92% of incoming requests that go through the edge.

Lee: UX note for Console: show a "View trace" button in the Logs table row when `redwood.trace_id` exists. Console should accept `?trace_id=` param and open the trace viewer; if trace not sampled show a clear "trace not sampled" state and link to the request in the trace explorer if available.

sre-oncall: Sampling policy: we keep full spans for sampled traces. But trace id can still be present on logs for unsampled traces. Console needs to handle that gracefully (show link -> "not sampled"). Also consider increasing sampling for canaries to ensure traces for new rollout issues.

Mike J: Action items agreed:
1) SDKs: inject `redwood.trace_id` from OTEL context by default (Anya)
2) Collector/Ingress: best-effort promote `traceparent` to `redwood.trace_id` for legacy apps (Devon + infra)
3) Indexing policy: default to index only ERROR+ or whitelist services (Lee)
4) Console: quick link UX + fallback state (Product/Console)
5) Instrument heuristics as last resort and mark inferred links (SRE)

Anya P: I'll draft the SDK PR by EOD and open a doc for the canonical field and examples. @Devon please post the collector config PR and tests.

Devon: Will take collector work — I'll add unit tests and a small e2e that simulates missing header -> no trace, header present -> `redwood.trace_id` added. Planning to roll to canary collectors next week.

Mike J: Thanks all — I'll open a GH epic with these tasks and link to the staging collector logs. If we can get SDKs + collector on staging that should resolve most canary failure investigations. :shipit:
